title: QUIC RFC 9368 Version Information Floor Work Item
summary: Close the RFC 9368 version_information floor by proving authenticated Version Information formatting, parsing, and snapshot preservation without claiming the full compatible-version runtime-selection flow.
planned_changes:
- Add `SPEC-QUIC-RFC9368.json`, `ARC-QUIC-RFC9368-0001.json`, `WI-QUIC-RFC9368-0001.json`, and `VER-QUIC-RFC9368-0001.json`.
- Keep `QuicVersionInformation` as the canonical transport-parameter snapshot shape and preserve it through the transport bridge, 0-RTT policy, and resumption store clone paths.
- Add requirement-home tests for authenticated Version Information formatting and malformed-value rejection, plus focused snapshot-preservation unit coverage where the cloned state is easiest to observe.
- Extend fuzz coverage so the transport-parameter parser and formatter exercise representative Version Information shapes.
- Extend transport-parameter benchmark coverage with explicit Version Information scenarios so the versioning floor shows up in the permanent hot-path suites.
- Keep the full compatible-version restart/selection flow out of scope for this slice and leave it in the gap ledger for a separate runtime-behavior pass.
verification_plan: Run the RFC 9368 requirement-home tests, run the transport-parameter codec and snapshot-preservation unit tests, run the transport-parameter benchmark dry run, validate SpecTrace JSON, refresh the QUIC requirement coverage triage, and run `git diff --check`.
out_of_scope: The full compatible-version restart/selection flow from RFC 9368 Section 4.
The QUIC v2 wire-format and cryptographic deltas from RFC 9369.
Higher-layer application adaptation for version negotiation beyond the authenticated transport-parameter floor.
completion_notes: Complete. The authenticated Version Information floor now has requirement-home, snapshot-preservation, fuzz, benchmark, and trace-validation evidence, while the compatible-version runtime follow-up remains separate.
